stories.headline: Was Pinarayi ministry earnest about rebuilding Kerala after 2018 floods? CAG says no
stories.title: Was Pinarayi ministry earnest about rebuilding Kerala after 2018 floods? CAG says no
stories.summary: A CAG report exposed severe irregularities in Kerala's post-flood road reconstruction projects, including unauthorised sub-contracting, fraudulent completion bonuses, and major contractual deviations that benefited contractors at public expense.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: After the apocalyptic destruction unleashed by the 2018 floods, the Pinarayi Vijayan government projected the Rebuild Kerala Initiative (RKI) as the embodiment of Kerala's resilience.
RKI was supposed to be the dedicated agency to coordinate and implement recovery and reconstruction efforts.
Its mandate was to adopt world-class ecology-sensitive technology to insulate Kerala against future disasters.
But how shoddily and carelessly such a fight back was mounted is revealed in the report of the Comptroller and Auditor General that was tabled in the Assembly on Tuesday.
It was as if resilience was forgotten the moment the waters receded.
Under RKI, 29 PWD roads with a total length of 718.94 km across 13 districts were selected for reconstruction, with a sanctioned cost of ₹5119.54 crore.
The CAG put the microscope on 10 of these roads.

The audit noticed deficiencies in the preparation of detailed project reports, bidding documents and several instances of deviation from contractual provisions, all of which ended up causing project delays, recurring design changes and undue benefit to contractors.
Take, for instance, how irresponsibly, and in utter violation of the contract clause, work on the Uravanchal-Maruthayi stretch in North Kerala was carried out.
Clause 3.2.1 of the Engineering Procurement and Construction (EPC) contract prohibits sub-contracting beyond 25 per cent of the contract price.
Clause 3.2.2 mandates prior intimation to the Authority if any sub-contract exceeds five per cent of the contract price.
Unauthorised sub-contracting constitutes ‘Contractor Default’ under Clause 23.1.1(i), and Clause 23.1.2 empowers the Authority to terminate the contract with 15 days' notice.

stories.title: Delhi High Court Directs Authorities To Provide Industrialist Anil Ambani's Son Details Of LOC Against Him
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Delhi High Court has directed the authorities to provide Jai Anshul Anil Ambani, son of industrialist Anil Ambani, specific details of the Look Out Circular (LOC) issued against him, including the date of its issuance, and a copy of the formal order.
Justice Mini Pushkarna passed the direction while hearing an application filed by Jai Anshul seeking compliance of an earlier order passed on September 17 by a coordinate bench.

The Court was informed that the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) had communicated to Jai Anshul on October 05 that an LOC had been issued against him in view of an ongoing investigation and that it continued to remain in force.
However, his counsel submitted that the communication was vague and did not disclose specific details regarding the LOC.
Taking note of the communication, the Court directed the authorities to provide details regarding when the LOC was issued and furnish a copy of the formal order to Jai Anshul in accordance with law.
The Court also took note of Ambani's submission that the communication was received only from the SFIO and not from the Bureau of Immigration.

“Accordingly, respondents are further directed to apprise the Court as to whether any other LOC has been issued against the petitioner, which is in the knowledge of the Bureau of Immigration,” the Court said.

During the hearing, counsel for the authorities submitted that the earlier direction had required the petition to be treated as a representation and requisite intimation to be provided within a time-bound manner.
It was argued that the Court had not directed the authorities to furnish specific details of the LOC.
The respondents also submitted that if Jai Anshul was dissatisfied with the communication issued by the SFIO, he could pursue other remedies available to him.
The matter will be considered next on October 16.

stories.headline: SC issues notice to Centre, ECI on plea challenging blanket immunity to CEC, ECs
stories.title: SC issues notice to Centre, ECI on plea challenging blanket immunity to CEC, ECs
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday issued notice to the Centre and the Election Commission of India (ECI) on a public interest litigation challenging the blanket immunity granted to the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and other Election Commissioners under Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and the other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The plea seeks revival of proceedings against current and past CEC/Election Commissioners.

The Supreme Court today issued notice on a petition filed by the Association for Democratic Reforms challenging the immunity granted to Chief Election Commissioner/Election Commissioners for actions taken in purported discharge of official duties.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana sought the response of the Union and the Election Commission on ADR's challenge to the constitutional validity of Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.
Senior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan appeared for ADR.
The petition has been filed through AoR Rani Mishra.
Briefly put, the petition seeks a declaration that Section 16 of the CEC Act is unconstitutional, void and inoperative as violative of Articles 14 and 21 and the basic structure of the Constitution.
It further seeks revival of proceedings against the present and past CEC and Election Commissioners, which came to an end as Section 16 of the CEC Act came into effect.

"Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, no Court shall entertain or continue any civil or criminal proceedings against any person who is or was a Chief Election Commissioner or an Election Commissioner for any act, thing or word, committed, done or spoken by him when, or in the course of acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty or function."
The petition contends that Section 16 provides blanket immunity to the current and previous CEC/ECs for lifetime, which has no rational nexus with the objective of ensuring independence of CEC/ECs.
The provision places the CEC & ECs beyond the reach of any Court of law, it highlights.
"No other provision in the Constitution of India or any statute grants immunity that is at once lifelong, unconditioned by good faith, free of any sanction mechanism, and without a saving clause."
Petitioner-ADR further points out that Section 16 was not originally part of the Bill introduced.

article_sentences: The Union government informed the Supreme Court on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) that its response to petitions alleging illegal detentions, shutdown of public and rail transport, including Metro service, in Delhi on October 10 is “ready” but needs more fine-tuning.
A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant extended the time for the government to file the reply affidavit by October 15.
Multiple petitions, including ones seeking contempt proceedings, were adjourned to October 15, 2026 as one of the judges on the Bench was unwell.
The Bench rose for the day shortly thereafter.
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, for the Centre, said he had gone through the prepared affidavit.
It was final, but he wanted to make it “more comprehensive”.

On the petitioners’ request, the Court asked him to share the affidavit, if possible, by October 14, 2026, a day before the hearing so that the lawyers of the petitioners were suitably well-versed with the contents of the affidavit and the hearing would be a meaningful one.

The Court also agreed to urgently hear fresh petitions seeking independent probe and contempt proceedings against authorities on the continued police action against journalists, especially women media professionals, covering the anti-CEC/SIR protests despite an apex court order against it on October 11.
Chief Justice Kant asked the petitioners to cure defects, after which the pleas would also be put up for a comprehensive hearing on Thursday (October 15, 2026).
The Court asked for a senior police officer to be present during the next hearing, when allegations of assault on women are raised in the courtroom.

Members of the Supreme Court Bar Association and Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association, of which petitions were adjourned on October 13, gathered at the Supreme Court lawns to express solidarity with the advocates who were assaulted and detained by the police during the October 10 and 11 protests.
A separate petition was orally mentioned by senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia about the “sad” incident which happened in the Supreme Court on October 12, 2026.

article_sentences: The petition filed by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and 10 prominent opposition leaders following a massive march on October 12 was not listed for hearing in the Supreme Court on Tuesday (October 13) as defects pointed out by the registry are yet to be cured.

As per the Supreme Court's website, the apex court registry had flagged 14 defects, including lack of a clear copy of the ID card of Congress president and Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge, a co-petitioner in the case.
The registry had also pointed out certain illegible or missing pages in the petition.

Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, in his response to Mr. Gandhi's request for a meeting to submit a memorandum on issues concerning the Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commission of India (ECI), the alleged arbitrary arrest of several students, closure of Metro stations and cancellation of trains, had assured early hearing of the plea, if filed, on the judicial side.
On Tuesday (October 13), a bench headed by the CJI assured the petitioners that their matters would be listed for hearing if the defects are cured.
"We will list all these matters.
Make sure that the defects are cured," the CJI told senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, who mentioned the matter on behalf of a journalist.

Besides Mr. Gandhi and Kharge, TMC MP Saugata Roy, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, Rashtriya Janata Dal leader Tejashwi Prasad Yadav, Nationalist Congress Party (Sharad Pawar) leader Supriya Sule, Shiv Sena-UBT leader Sanjay Raut, Communist Party of India's D. Raja, Jharkhand Mukti Morcha MP Mahua Majhi, CPI(M) general secretary M.A. Baby and Indian Union Muslim League leader E.T. Mohammed Basheer are co-petitioners in the plea filed by the Congress leader.
The plea has alleged large-scale voter deletions and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

It has sought the constitution of an independent committee, headed by a retired apex court judge and assisted by technical experts and other citizens of eminence, to conduct a time-bound, independent audit of deletions and modifications made during the SIR.

It has also sought a direction to ensure that no elector is deleted from the electoral rolls without notice and a reasonable opportunity of hearing in accordance with the law, and also to ensure that eligible persons in Punjab and other states going to polls are permitted to seek inclusion in the electoral rolls until the last date permitted by law.

"Issue an interim direction suspending the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls across the states, pending consideration and adjudication of the issues raised in the present petition, in the interests of protecting the rights of eligible electors and preserving the integrity of the electoral process," the plea said.

stories.title: How the weight loss market is prompting pharma biggies to look at India afresh
stories.summary: Eli Lilly has a “follow-the-sun” model for its research and development wing, which gets 20 to 25 cents of every dollar from its sales revenue. Under this model, drug development never stops, with work on new drugs ticking round the clock across centres in the United States, Europe, and India.“Lilly has become the fastest developer of drugs in the world. One of the reasons for that is a follow-the-sun model. The work actually never stops on any pipeline product. We do it round the clock. article_sentences: The Supreme Court has agreed to hear a plea against Section 16 of the 2023 election law.
The challenge says the provision gives election commissioners sweeping lifelong immunity from proceedings.

The Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to hear a plea challenging the validity of a provision in a 2023 law that grants immunity to the chief election commissioner and election commissioners for certain acts carried out in the discharge of their official duties.

A bench of the Supreme Court comprising Justices Surya Kant, Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice to the Centre and the Election Commission on the plea filed by NGO Association for Democratic Reforms.
The court also tagged the matter with a separate pending petition that raises a similar issue.
The plea has sought to have Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 declared unconstitutional.

Section 16 of the law says, "Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, no court shall entertain or continue any civil or criminal proceedings against any person who is or was a Chief Election Commissioner or an Election Commissioner for any act, thing or word, committed, done or spoken by him when, or in the course of acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty or function."

In January this year, the top court had agreed to examine a separate plea challenging the immunity granted to the chief election commissioner and the election commissioners under Section 16 of the 2023 Act.
It had then issued notice to the Centre and the Election Commission on a plea filed by NGO Lok Prahari, but refused to stay the provision.

The latest plea said the provision "gives unprecedented, unbridled power to the CEC and ECs by providing them complete blanket permanent immunity for life from any civil and even criminal proceedings for their wrongdoings in gross misuse of their office".
With the new plea now before it and linked to the earlier case, the Supreme Court has sought responses from the Centre and the Election Commission on the challenge to Section 16 of the 2023 law.

The Supreme Court on Tuesday declined to entertain a plea alleging that personnel of the Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad entered the petitioner's residence without wearing proper uniforms or displaying identification.
The bench said the petitioner should first seek relief from the Allahabad High Court.
A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said it was not inclined to hear the matter at the first instance as petitioner.
Waiz Khan had directly moved the top court under Article 32 of the Constitution.
The court dismissed the plea, while giving him the liberty to approach the high court.

"If I am coming under Article 32, the Supreme Court can't (shy away)," the counsel said.

Justice Bagchi, however, said Articles 32 and 226 of the Constitution provide overlapping jurisdiction in matters involving alleged violations of fundamental rights, and that the court of first instance should ordinarily be allowed to examine such allegations.

Justice Bagchi said, "We would always prefer a court of first instance to take cognisance of violation of fundamental rights." The petitioner's counsel also referred to the Supreme Court's landmark judgment in D K Basu vs State of West Bengal, which laid down safeguards against custodial abuse and illegal arrest.
Justice Bagchi, however, pointed to the remedies available before the high court in cases involving alleged violations of personal liberty.

It had passed the order on a plea filed by Mr. Suryavanshi's wife and children challenging an October 2024 order of the Chhattisgarh High Court, which held that he was subjected to custodial violence and died as a result thereof.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Adjourns Delhi Protest Matter To October 15
stories.title: Supreme Court Adjourns Delhi Protest Matter To October 15
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: The Supreme Court today adjourned to October 15 the pleas filed relating to protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Election Commission's SIR of electoral rolls.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was scheduled to hear the matter today, but considering Justice Mohana's ill-health, the parties expressed that they had no objection if the matters were taken up on October 15.
Senior Advocates Gopal Sankaranarayanan, Menaka Guruswamy, Arundhati Katju, CU Singh, Nitya Ramakrishnan, Indira Jaising, and Solicitor General Tushar Mehta appeared.
The Court sought the presence of a senior Delhi police officer to respond to the plea of women journalists alleging police assault during protest coverage.

On the SG's request, the Court extended the time till October 15 for filing of a compliance report pursuant to the Court's October 9 directions and the response to Shailendra Mani Tripathi's contempt petition and Dr Menaka Guruswamy's petition.

Notice was also issued today on a fresh petition filed by the Association for Democratic Reforms challenging Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioners and Other Election Commissioners Act 2023, which provides immunity to ECs for actions taken in discharge of official duties.

In a special sitting on October 11, the Court directed that there shall be no detention of any person except in accordance with the procedure established by law, particularly with respect to any assembly of peaceful and unarmed persons beyond the area where Section 163 BNSS prohibitory orders are in operation.

A bench of Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana also directed the authorities to take down the board concerning the imposition of Section 163 of BNSS in the area around the Supreme Court, if not already done, to ensure there was no apprehension regarding access to justice, including ingress and egress to any court of law.

The Court further directed that metro and rail facilities shall function normally unless restrictions are required to be imposed keeping in mind disturbances to public order, as contemplated under Article 19(2) of the Constitution of India.

On the movement of people, the Court directed that free movement in the city be permitted subject to traffic regulations and lawyers, journalists, other professionals be not impeded in discharging their professional duties.
It further ordered that the imposition of barricades be reviewed forthwith, keeping in mind law and order and other traffic conditions.
It was also directed that internet services shall remain undisturbed in the city.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Tuesday sought inputs from the Intelligence Bureau (IB) on whether Jagtar Singh Hawara, convicted in the 1995 assassination of former Punjab Chief Minister Beant Singh, can be transferred from Tihar Jail in Delhi to a prison in Punjab, after concerns raised by the Punjab government over the possible impact on law and order.

A bench of Justice MM Sundresh and Justice PB Varale was hearing Hawara's plea seeking transfer to a jail in Punjab, primarily to enable him to meet his elderly mother, who is stated to be in serious condition.
The Court said that it would consider the request after obtaining the IB's assessment of the potential security and law-and-order implications of the transfer.
The Court observed that it could not disregard the Punjab government's objections, particularly since the case involved concerns that went beyond the individual prisoner.
It said that while it was inclined to consider such requests sympathetically, it had to ensure that its order did not trigger further problems in the state.
Justice Sundresh observed that the case could not be treated as an ordinary murder case because the state had raised concerns about the continuing influence of the ideology associated with the crime.

stories.headline: SC questions Delhi Police over alleged assault on women journalists
stories.title: SC questions Delhi Police over alleged assault on women journalists
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 13 : The Supreme Court on Tuesday took serious note of allegations that women journalists covering protests in the national capital were assaulted by police personnel and directed a senior Delhi Police officer to remain present during the hearing on Thursday to explain the matter. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana made the observation after senior advocate Indira Jaising mentioned a petition filed by the Network of Women in Media, India (NWMI), seeking safeguards for journalists covering protests, particularly women journalists. "We would like some senior officer to remain present here and explain," the CJI Kant-led Bench said, indicating that the police would have to explain the allegations. The development comes amid allegations that journalists covering protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar were manhandled, detained and obstructed while discharging their professional duties on October 10 and 11. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan also mentioned a separate contempt petition alleging that the police had assaulted journalists in violation of the Supreme Court’s October 10 order. The apex court had directed the authorities to ensure that lawyers, journalists and other professionals were not hindered in discharging their professional duties. The directions were passed by a Bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana while hearing contempt petitions alleging violations of its order concerning restrictions imposed ahead of the proposed protest. It had also directed the authorities to ensure the normal functioning of Metro and railway services, uninterrupted internet connectivity and free movement of people, subject to traffic regulations and public order requirements. The Supreme Court had also directed that there should be no detention except in accordance with the procedure established by law, particularly in the case of peaceful and unarmed gatherings outside areas where prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were in force. --IANS

stories.title: IMD: Heavy rain in Keralam, South Karnataka, TN, Puducherry for 4 days from Thursday
stories.summary: Watch for low-pressure system over south-east Bay of Bengal withdrawn after parent circulation disappears, but South Peninsula is entering a consequential wet phase in seasonal calendar
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The South Peninsula is bracing for the arrival of the north-east monsoon, with the seasonal reversal of winds expected to gather momentum alongside the retreat of the south-west monsoon.

The trigger could be a low-pressure area forecast to develop over the south-east Bay of Bengal anytime now, setting the stage for the easterly flows that herald the onset of the second rainy season for the water-starved region.
The atmospheric signals are falling into place, with an upper-air cyclonic circulation over the South Andaman Sea poised to descend to lower levels and consolidate into the crucial low-pressure area.
At the western end of the Bay, another cyclonic circulation over the Gulf of Mannar could help draw in and channel the easterly winds, carrying the north-east monsoon deeper into the South Peninsula.
With the Bay of Bengal primed for a fresh low-pressure system and the retreating monsoon nearing its final exit, the South Peninsula is entering a consequential phase of the seasonal calendar.

The coming days will determine how quickly the easterlies take charge, and whether the expected onset of north-east monsoon brings a sustained spell of rain to the region after the south-west monsoon’s long retreat.
The emerging weather pattern is already offering a foretaste of the transition, with rain, thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds unfolding over several parts of southern India.
These conditions could intensify on either side of October 15, around which the north-east monsoon is likely to set in over Tamil Nadu and adjoining areas.
Its formal arrival could be announced during this phase.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD), in its Tuesday morning assessment, said conditions were becoming favourable for the south-west monsoon to withdraw from the remaining parts of the country and for north-east monsoon rains to commence over the South Peninsula simultaneously during the next 2-3 days.
The withdrawal line of the four-month south-west monsoon, which officially ended on September 30, continues to pass through Kolkata, Angul, Khammam and Honavar.
The predecessor monsoon must complete its retreat from the mainland before the seasonal transition is fully established, although the two processes can overlap in time.
